camps.name: Upper Ferry Basin / Ferry Glacial Lake
camps.why: The only camp on this plan that reports confirm: meadow and tarn ground under Mount Ferry, with water, reached on the third day of the traverse.

camps.name: Elwha Basin, Queets Basin and the upper cross-country bivy zones
camps.why: Belongs to the approach from Whiskey Bend up the Elwha, not to this Sol Duc traverse; use it only if you come in from the south.

camps.name: Lillian River and Mary's Falls — the first night out of Whiskey Bend
camps.why: First-night camp on the Elwha approach from Whiskey Bend. Not slept at on this Sol Duc plan.

camps.name: Hayes River and Elkhorn — the mid-valley camps, and the base for Mount Norton
camps.why: Mid-valley Elwha camp on the Whiskey Bend approach, or on the way out if the final day is split. Not on the Sol Duc plan's nights.

camps.name: Chicago Camp — the last established camp in the upper Elwha
camps.why: Last trail camp on the Elwha. The plan reaches it only on its final walk-out day, so it matters if you split that day.

plan_conflict: Nights 4 and 5 sleep in a meadow near Bear Pass, and nights 1 and 2 at Cat Basin and Stephen Lake, none of which is a camp on file; the on-file Elwha Basin camp is for the other approach, so it is no longer main.

camps.name: Ferry Basin
camps.why: Meadow and tarn basin directly below Mount Ferry. Parties drop packs here and scramble the peak, so it is the natural second night of the traverse.

camps.name: Deer Lake
camps.why: Short first day on the Sol Duc trail, well below the High Divide; it leaves a longer cross-country day to reach Ferry Basin.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 at Heart Lake and night 3 in Queets Basin; the accounts found pass Heart Lake or stop elsewhere, and no account confirms Queets Basin or a Low Divide trail camp on nights 3 and 4.

camps.name: Heart Lake
camps.why: Last dependable water before the ridge and the planned first camp. A few parties walk on to the Cat Peak ridge instead, which makes the next day shorter.

camps.name: Ferry Basin
camps.why: Meadow and tarns under Mount Ferry. The usual camp for Pulitzer and Ferry, since both peaks are an early-morning scramble from here.

camps.name: Upper Ferry Basin camp
camps.why: Higher camp up the basin near the glacial lake, a little closer to the peaks. Some parties pick it over the lower meadows for the shorter morning.

plan_conflict: The plan has night 3 in Queets Basin and night 4 on the upper Elwha; accounts found camp near Bear Pass or at Hayes River, so those nights are not confirmed, and Heart Lake as night 1 is passed by some parties.

camps.name: Hayes River and Elkhorn — the mid-valley camps, and the base for Mount Norton
camps.why: Level riverside camps in the mid Elwha valley, about halfway to Chicago Camp. A sensible first night, and the place most parties sleep again coming out.

camps.name: Elwha Basin, Queets Basin and the upper cross-country bivy zones
camps.why: Cross-country camp above the maze, within reach of Dodwell-Rixon Pass. It lets the summit day be a light carry from the tent.

camps.name: Lillian River and Mary's Falls — the first night out of Whiskey Bend
camps.why: Closer camp near the start of the valley; choose it if the road walk or a late start makes the first day short.

camps.name: Chicago Camp — the last established camp in the upper Elwha
camps.why: Last trail camp before the cross-country begins. Parties stopping here give up the basin camp and take a longer summit day.

camps.name: Low Divide — the pass camp for Mount Seattle and Mount Christie
camps.why: Flat, watered pass camp with a toilet, a short walk from the peak's scree lines. Parties usually sleep here both nights rather than carry higher.

camps.name: Seattle Meadows
camps.why: Higher meadow camp nearer the summit scramble, but with little standing water and more carrying than Low Divide.

camps.name: Lillian River and Mary's Falls — the first night out of Whiskey Bend
camps.why: Camp on the Elwha side of Low Divide, not on this Quinault approach; it matters only if you cross the divide.

camps.name: Hayes River and Elkhorn — the mid-valley camps, and the base for Mount Norton
camps.why: Elwha-side valley camp, far from this Quinault approach. Not slept at on this plan.

camps.name: Chicago Camp — the last established camp in the upper Elwha
camps.why: Elwha-side trail camp below Low Divide; used only by parties crossing the divide from the south.

plan_conflict: Low Divide is main on file and the plan sleeps nights 2 and 3 at the high camp; Seattle Meadows is moved to route. Nights 1 and 4 on the North Fork Quinault have no camp on file.

camps.name: Home Lake, below Constance Pass — inside the park, and reached from the north
camps.why: The high camp on this side, about nine miles in. The buttress is a day from the tent and the plan returns to it, so both nights are here.

camps.name: Boulder Shelter — the last camp outside the national park
camps.why: Free, unbooked camp lower on the trail; saves distance on day one but adds a long, brushy carry to the climb.

new_camps.name: Home Lake
new_camps.why: The camp the plan uses: about nine miles up the Upper Dungeness trail, and the climb is a day trip from here with a return to the same tent.
new_camps.notes: Elevation is taken from the figure other routes on file use for the same lake. No report of this route was found, so the nights come from the plan alone.

camps.name: Home Lake
camps.why: Standard camp for this side of the mountain; Constance Pass is a short climb above, so the summit day starts close to the tent.

camps.name: Camp Handy
camps.why: Low, sheltered, permit-free camp three miles in. Parties use it for a very short first day or a slow walk out.

camps.name: Boulder Shelter
camps.why: Six miles in at the trail junction; a cheaper night than Home Lake, with a longer summit day.

plan_conflict: Accounts found camp in Deception Basin, reached from the Royal Basin side, as the closest camp to Fricaba; few parties use Home Lake.

camps.name: Flapjack Lakes — the base camp for the whole Sawtooth Ridge
camps.why: Base camp for the whole Sawtooth Ridge, with water and a quota system. Parties often stay both nights and climb from here.

camps.name: Black and White Lakes — the fallback when Flapjack is booked out
camps.why: The fallback when Flapjack is booked out; higher and farther from the ridge, which lengthens the summit day.

plan_conflict: The plan moves night 2 to a primitive camp near Gladys Divide, which is not on file; only Flapjack Lakes is on file, and Black and White Lakes changes from main to route.

camps.name: Conrad Meadows and Surprise Lake, South Fork Tieton
camps.why: Wooded, sheltered camp on the trail in; a longer summit day than Warm Lake, which sits higher and in wind above the trees.

plan_conflict: The plan offers Surprise Lake or Warm Lake; accounts of Gilbert show both used, with Warm Lake common for the summit, but none states where Meade Glacier parties sleep, and Warm Lake is not on file.

camps.name: Avalanche Glacier high bivy
camps.why: Dry high camp above 9,000 ft on the ridge beside the glacier. It cuts the summit day short but has little water; carry or melt.

camps.name: Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead
camps.why: Car camp at the trailhead: the night before, or the last night on a slow descent. Not a camp on the plan's nights.

camps.name: Lunch Counter
camps.why: The South Climb high camp. A fall-back if you give up on the Avalanche side and descend south.

camps.name: Morrison Creek Campground
camps.why: Lower drive-in campground for when the road or Cold Springs is full; it adds a long approach day.

plan_conflict: The on-file role of Cold Springs as main does not match the plan, which sleeps nights 1 and 2 at a high camp near Mad Cat Meadow or Salt Creek; neither is on file, and no account of the route's camps was found.

camps.name: Avalanche Valley
camps.why: Meadow basin right under the Rusk and Wilson glaciers, the closest camp to the headwall; it puts the climb a short alpine start away.

camps.name: Cold Springs / South Climb trailhead
camps.why: South Climb trailhead; the descent ends here, and a few parties sleep here before the long traverse.

plan_conflict: The notes on file reach Avalanche Valley from Bird Creek Meadows or the Highline Trail, but the plan starts at Cold Springs and walks round the east flank; no account of either was found.

camps.name: Edmunds/North Mowich glacier divide camp
camps.why: Parties put both nights at this 8,100 ft camp on the divide between the two glaciers, and climb the face and return to it.

camps.name: Ptarmigan Ridge bivy above Observation Rock
camps.why: Sheltered rock windbreaks, but you must still descend scree onto the North Mowich; some parties use it as their only camp.

camps.name: High camp below the North Mowich headwall
camps.why: Closest to the face but exposed to icefall and rockfall; worth it only in cold, stable conditions.

camps.name: Liberty Cap saddle
camps.why: Emergency bivy for a party benighted after topping out, not a planned camp.

plan_conflict: The plan moves to a higher bivy on night 2, but the reports found stay at the 8,100 ft divide camp for every night; the on-file Ptarmigan Ridge bivy changes from main to route.

camps.name: Nisqually Glacier camp below the icefall
camps.why: On the upper glacier or its moraine, so the icefall is crossed before sunrise. The site moves with the year.

camps.name: Camp Muir
camps.why: Easier ground and a shelter, used by the first-ascent party; the drop to the icefall costs height and time before dawn.

camps.name: Ingraham Flats
camps.why: Higher bench above Muir, colder and exposed to icefall; not a normal night for this route.

camps.name: Colonnade Ridge
camps.why: First stopping point after the Wonderland Trail, around 6,700 ft: a snow camp that sets up the cleaver the next morning.

camps.name: Bergschrund camp in the Sunset Amphitheater
camps.why: Good ground by a small schrund at the top of the amphitheater gully, reached from the cleaver; sited well, it cuts the summit day.

camps.name: Puyallup Cleaver high camp
camps.why: Rib camp around 9,000 ft before the glacier traverse; exposed to wind, and it leaves a longer day than the schrund camp.

camps.name: Open bivouac near 9,600 ft
camps.why: Committing open bivouac to shorten summit day; it only pays off with good snow on the face.

plan_conflict: Night 3 (Camp Schurman or Camp Muir) has no camp on file and no Sunset Ridge report confirms it, and the plan's South Mowich Glacier camp is closest to the on-file Bergschrund camp, now main for night 2.

camps.name: Puyallup Cleaver camp below St. Andrews Rock
camps.why: Flat sites at the base of the rocks, just short of the ramp onto the Tahoma Glacier; summit day goes from the tent and returns to it.

new_camps.name: St. Andrews Park camp, Wonderland Trail
new_camps.why: Timberline bench with a pond below the cleaver; the usual first night, which makes the move to high camp a short half day.
new_camps.notes: Meadow camp on the Wonderland Trail reached by the South Puyallup River trail. Height is the high point listed for the St. Andrews Lake hike.

camps.name: Curtis Ridge camp
camps.why: The camp the climb is made from: leave before midnight to reach the cones while the wall above is frozen.

camps.name: Glacier Basin camp
camps.why: Camp on the White River approach with last running water; a shorter first day, then a long carry to Curtis Ridge.

camps.name: St Elmo Pass bivy
camps.why: Staging bivy at the pass for parties who start late and cannot reach Curtis Ridge in daylight.

new_camps.name: Camp Schurman
new_camps.why: The ranger camp where the descent from the wall ends, with tent sites and shelter after a very long day.
new_camps.notes: Reached by descending the Emmons-Winthrop after the climb. Height is the figure the Mountaineers route page gives.

plan_conflict: Day 2 ends at Camp Schurman, which is not on file, so it is added as the night 2 main; no account of this route's second night was found.
